description:
Satvis is a free, open-source satellite tracker for iPhone and iPad. It draws more than 16,000 satellites on a 3D globe in real time: Starlink, GPS, weather satellites, the ISS and many more. Set your location and it predicts when each one passes overhead. The sky view shows the sky from where you stand. Point your phone up to see the satellites in that direction.

WHAT IT DOES
• Visualize more than 16,000 satellites on a 3D globe in real time, propagated on the device with SGP4 from CelesTrak's element sets
• Show points, labels, orbits, orbit tracks, ground tracks, sensor cones, 3D models and ground station links per satellite, coloured by orbit class (LEO, MEO, GEO, HEO)
• Switch catalog groups on and off (Starlink, GNSS, weather, Earth observation, crewed stations), or search for a single satellite
• Select a satellite to see its orbit, its next passes and its spacecraft details: country, operator, manufacturer, bus, mass and size
• Track a satellite: the camera flies to it and follows it along its orbit
• Set ground stations from your location or a point you pick on the map, then list their upcoming passes and get a notification before one starts
• Find satellites in the sky overhead in a ground-level sky view you aim by dragging, or by pointing your phone
• See which satellites you could spot: the sky view dims those in Earth's shadow, too far away or in a daylit sky
• Lay the globe over the base map and terrain you choose: satellite imagery, Earth at night or the day's VIIRS imagery
• Start from the demo views, bookmark your own, and share any view as a link: it opens the same view on satvis.space
• Open satvis.space links straight in the app
• Keep using it offline, from the satellite data it last fetched

WHERE THE DATA COMES FROM
Orbital elements come from CelesTrak, refreshed several times a day, and are propagated on your device with SGP4. What each satellite is comes from Jonathan McDowell's GCAT.

FREE AND OPEN SOURCE
No account, no ads, no in-app purchases. Developed in the open at github.com/Flowm/satvis under the MIT licence.
whatsNew:
Satvis 2.0 is a new app. Earlier versions showed the satvis.space web page in a frame; this one is built natively for iPhone and iPad, and draws its own 3D globe.

• The sky view: look up from where you are, aim by moving your phone, and see which satellites are sunlit against a dark sky
• Passes over your saved locations, listed as they are found, with a notification before each one starts
• 3D models of the satellites, and a camera that flies to a satellite and follows it
• What each satellite is: country, operator, manufacturer, mass and size
• Bookmarks: demo views to start from, your own saved views, and a link to share any of them
• satvis.space links open in the app
• Satellite imagery, Earth at night, today's VIIRS imagery and terrain
• Works offline from the satellite data it last fetched
• The menus of satvis.space, beside the globe on iPhone and open on iPad
